newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Hungary, Slovakia move towards treaty committees.
newsitem.headline: Hungary, Slovakia move towards treaty committees.

text.p: Hungary and Slovakia have moved to set up committees to implement a friendship treaty they signed this year to ease strained relations, Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said on Saturday.
Kovacs said he and Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik agreed in talks during a Central European summit in Austria that Slovakia would respond to the proposal by the end of this month.

"We agreed that by the end of November they will give an answer to my proposal to establish a joint committee co-chaired by the two foreign ministers -- and with as many subcommittees or working groups as the Slovak party wants -- to follow the implementation of the basic treaty," Kovacs said.

Relations between Slovakia and Hungary are strained because of differences over Slovakia's treatment of its 500,000-strong Hungarian minority. Progress was achieved this year when Slovakia signed a basic friendship treaty with Hungary.

Kovacs said Hungary and Slovakia also agreed to extend until the end of the year talks to try to reach an out-of-court settlement on their long-running dispute over the controversial Slovak Gabcikovo dam project on the Danube river.
"We agreed that we would continue the expert-level talks which is to explore the possibility to come to an agreement out of The Hague treaty if possible," Kovacs said.
The two countries' dispute over the dam, which originally was a joint project until Hungary backed out, has been submitted to the International Court of Justice at The Hague.
"We will not reveal any details because we do not want to make or have any impact on The Hague -- and we have not withdrawn it (our court pleading)," Kovacs said.
"But we are trying to find a solution outside The Hague and we just agreed that we would prolong the talks to the end of the year."
